subject: Simple beta_binomial regression results in many divergent transitions

messages.author: b30c14c8b83478cb
messages.subject: Simple beta_binomial regression results in many divergent transitions
parts:
Hello,

I've coded up what I believe is a pretty straightforward beta-binomial model, but when I run it I get almost as many divergent transitions as there are post-warmup draws (e.g. 996 of 1000). So the effective sample size ends up being around 4-6 for each parameter and the results don't make sense. I've tried increasing adapt_delta to 0.95 without luck. If I simplify the specification further however, say by removing the age covariate, the model runs fine. The final model will include a variety of covariates and will be a multilevel model though, so this is a just a simplified model which I'll be building up. Any ideas what might be going on here?

Thanks!


data {
    int N;
    int y[N];
    int yTotal[N];
    real dist[N];
    real avgDensity[N];
    real age[N];
}

parameters {
    real<lower = 0> phi;
    real alpha;
    real beta_distance;
    real beta_avgDensity;
    real beta_age;
}

model {
    vector[N] lambda;
    vector[N] a;
    vector[N] b;

    // Priors
    phi ~ gamma(1, 1);

    alpha ~ normal(0, 5);
    beta_distance ~ normal(0, 5);
    beta_avgDensity ~ normal(0, 5);
    beta_age ~ normal(0, 5);

    // Likelihood
    for(i in 1:N) {
        lambda[i] <- inv_logit(alpha +
                     beta_distance * dist[i] +

                     beta_avgDensity * avgDensity[i] +
                     beta_age * age[i]);
        a[i] <- lambda[i] * phi;
        b[i] <- (1 - lambda[i]) * phi;
    }

    y ~ beta_binomial(yTotal, a, b);
}

The final model will include a variety of covariates and will be a multilevel model though, so this is a just a simplified model which I'll be building up. Any ideas what might be going on here?

Yeah, as a first guess I think the prior distributions of "a" and "b" are screwy.  If you want to check that drop the "y ~ ..." statement and use the generated quantities block to record a/b values (so a model with no data, just simulating from the prior).  You'll likely get something very strange (0/phi, mostly, I think).  The issue is exacerbated with having a sum of independent but very weak priors piped through inv_logit.    I don't know if there are other issues---I think you constrained all the things that need constraining other than that. 

Krzysztof

Thanks!

    int N;
    int y[N];
    int yTotal[N];
    real dist[N];

    real age[N];
}

parameters {

    // Priors

    alpha ~ normal(0, 5);

    // Likelihood

    y ~ beta_binomial(yTotal, a, b);

parts:
Hi Krzysztof and Bob,

Thanks very much for your comments.

I've been able to figure out a way around the odd behavior. I noticed in the manual under "20. Optimizing Stan Code" that model speed can be increased by mean-centering and standardizing predictors. This didn't seem related to the model fitting problem, but I coded it up in the "transform data" block in any case. The model can now be fit without any problems. I've added in a full set of predictors now, and have a multilevel specification set up for a wide array of groups. So I more or less just stumbled on a solution. I don't have any intuition for why this would have helped, although I suspect the two of you might.
